input.content: The legacy importer can emit inverted windows (end < start); these used to pass through merge_windows as-is and became nonsense schedule entries. Fixed by mapping every input through Window::normalised (swaps bounds when end < start) BEFORE the (start, end) sort, so the sort-order invariant the merge loop depends on still holds and inverted windows merge with whatever they overlap after normalisation. Any new entry point that feeds windows into the merge must normalise first (or reuse merge_windows) — comparing raw importer windows with overlaps() gives wrong answers for inverted ones.

content.text:
Done — `cargo test --test primary_test_2` passes.

What I changed in `src/scheduling.rs`:

- Added `Window::normalised()` (src/scheduling.rs:19), which returns the window with bounds swapped when `end < start` and a copy of itself otherwise.
- `merge_windows` now normalises every input window before sorting (src/scheduling.rs:38), so inverted windows from the legacy importer become their normalised form and merge with anything they overlap.

Before touching the code I used `recall` on `merge_windows`, which surfaced an invariant: the merge loop only extends `last.end` and is correct solely because inputs are sorted by `(start, end)` first. That's why the fix normalises *before* the sort rather than patching the loop — a raw inverted window would break both the sort order and `overlaps()`. I recorded this fix as a `bughistory` memory anchored to `merge_windows` so future work knows importer windows must be normalised before comparison.
